Verified on 45/45 KN5000 files

notes: FILE: "KN5000 SOUND RAM" (16 B, checked at boot by SendPartDataBlock_ClearByte4 0xFEF950) + 40 x 470-B sound records at 0x10 + 470*n (MEMORY A 1..20, B 1..20) + the user-kit tail at 0x4980 (not 0x4990: 16 + 40*470 = 0x4980; the kit NAME is its first 16 B). The tail is 295-B kit header + 128 x 80-B user drum instruments + 1-B edit index + 2-B checksum; the checksum covers only 0x10..0x497F. RECORD = the subcpu tone-record format (table_data/tone_database_records.s, 21 + 81*N with N = 5) at its full 426 B: head +0x00..+0x14, common block +0x15..+0x65, four partial blocks +0x66 + 81*p; DSP_Reinit_VoiceSlots 0x035323 copies the 40 ROM staging streams (tone table indices 338-377) into the RAM image as 426 B each = the factory defaults; then 44 B = four 11-B velocity-split records, the RAM copy of the ToneDB_MixerDefaultTable record a ROM tone would look up. The task note "factory defaults at v10 file offset 0x0A0150 (0x72A6 B)" does not hold: 0x0A0150 (0xEA0150) is only the 16-B header string; the 426-B SoundRam_DefaultRecord 0xEED59D ("    Initial     ") is what SoundRam_FillDefaultRecord 0xFEFD28 puts under converted KN1500/KN2000 records, and the 40 factory sounds come from table_data via the subcpu. The clamp tables (ParamSx_*) give a (min, max, value_mask) per offset; they are range ARGUMENTS of the call at 0xFEEE06 -> 0xFEEC3F, whose body as decoded (ld HL,WA; cpl BC; and HL,BC; retd 4) does not apply them, so they document the intended ranges rather than enforce them; "observed.in_clamp_range" tests them on the corpus. KINDS: signed = int8 two's complement unless "bias" is 64 (stored value - 64). bits = flags/packed fields named in evidence. REPEAT: a field with repeat {count, stride} stands for count copies at off + k*stride, named <name>_<k>. Field tiling of both blocks is checked by gen_tm_spec.py (every byte exactly once after repeat expansion). Old-format images: SoundRam_ConvertUserSounds 0xFF024E dispatches on the 16-B id (SoundRam_Id_KN2000 / MKA / MKB / KN3000 / KN1500 / KN5000); KN3000 images lack the kit +0x11 byte (SoundRam_ConvertKn3000DrumKit 0xFF03FB inserts it), KN1500 records are 289 B (SoundRam_ConvertKn1500Record 0xFEF9B4), KN2000/MKA/MKB 144 B (SoundRam_ConvertKn2000Record 0xFEFD77).
